en: Preface to the Genealogy of the Buddhas and Patriarchs:
Tsk! Before the very beginning, was there ever such news?

Without this crew of fellows, there would have been no causeless dividing of lineages and establishing of schools upon a mere hair-tip, setting one against another; they were already incompetent from the start, defiling the purity.

[The respondent] said: "How could one possibly add a point to an arrow? To commit this to ink and paper and circulate it under a title—this would be improper. However, matters do not always follow a single direction;

as the saying goes, 'If the ancestors cannot settle their own affairs, the calamity will reach their descendants. As for our Elder Śākyamuni, what was transmitted by one person as a fiction was transmitted by ten thousand people as a reality.
From that time on, there were the four groups and seven patriarchs in India, and the two or three [patriarchs] in this land; from these came Dajian [Huineng], who emerged from Nanyue and Qingyuan."

The two branches of the *Chen* and *Ying* lineages are like tender cassia sprouts. In the fourth generation, the Guiyang school appeared; in the fifth, the Linji school; in the sixth, the Caodong school;
in the seventh, the Yunmen school; and in the ninth, the Fayan school.

Lamp after lamp continues the flame, and branch after branch reflects its brilliance. Whether they were transmitted or ceased, whether orthodox or collateral, they are all— [...all are... (the text ends here).
"A single drop of water from the Cao Yuan (Cao Creek) source. Since the *Denglu Huiyuan* (The Source of the Lamp Records), several hundred years have now passed;
yet among the two or three authors who have compiled [the records], there have been no small errors and omissions. I could not help but follow their patterns like one painting a gourd after another.

Thus, I have consulted each and every work, including the *Chuan Deng Zong Tu Xuji* (Continued Collection of the Genealogy of the Lamp School). Indeed, it is difficult to conceal the crooked with the straight. Therefore, I have arranged them again according to the original origins of the Five Schools.

I have examined this in detail and revised it further, bringing it forth once again not for the sake of competing for aesthetic splendor, but merely so that these words may circulate throughout the world.
Should those of future generations with ears hear them and those with eyes see them, it will be no small matter. Perhaps some man might come forward and say:
"All sentient beings in the entire universe—whom among them is not his own kindred grass? You seem to think it is only this [limited thing]."
"Are these masters continuing the Buddha’s life-force of wisdom? Jinyin Ming simply said to him: "The Eye of the True Dharma breaks the sand bowl.

The Primal Patriarch, Śākyamuni Buddha, appeared as the fourth honored one of the Bhadrakalpa.

He was born in the kingdom of Central India into the Kṣatriya caste; Śākya was his clan name. His father was King Śuddhodana, and his mother was Queen Māyā. On the eighth day of the fourth month in the year of Jiayin, the ninth year of King Zhao of the Zhou dynasty, he was born.

He renounced the rank of a Cakravartin Universal Monarch to leave the household life, realize the Unsurpassed Way, and turn the Great Dharma Wheel. Ninety-seven years later, as he was about to enter Parinirvāṇa at Kuśinagara, he entrusted the Treasury of the Eye of the True Dharma to Mahākāśyapa. During the reign of King Mu...

On the fifteenth day of the second month in the sixteenth year, the Ren-shen year, he entered parinirvāṇa at midnight. One thousand and seventeen years later, the teaching reached the land of China; this was the tenth year of the Yongping era of Emperor Ming of the Han, the Ding-mao year.
